title: Torque & Static Equilibrium
description: Investigate lever arms, principle of moments, rotational equilibrium of a seesaw, and beam center of gravity

variables.m1Desc: Mass of the load placed on the left side of the seesaw
variables.x1Desc: Distance of the left mass from the pivot (negative denotes leftward)
variables.m2Desc: Mass of the load placed on the right side of the seesaw
variables.x2Desc: Distance of the right mass from the pivot (positive denotes rightward)
variables.beamMassDesc: Mass of the seesaw beam distributed along its full length
variables.pivotOffsetDesc: Distance of the fulcrum relative to beam center; non-zero value creates self-weight torque
variables.frictionDesc: Rotational friction and damping at the fulcrum axle in real mode

presets.perfectBalanceDesc: Balancing unequal masses using reciprocal lever arm lengths (net torque = 0)
presets.equalArmsDesc: Classic symmetric equilibrium with identical torques on both sides
presets.heavyShortArm: Heavy Weight on Short Arm (12kg @ 0.5m vs 3kg @ 2m)
presets.heavyShortArmDesc: Lifting heavy loads by applying effort along a longer lever arm
presets.shiftedFulcrumDesc: Explore self-weight torque when the fulcrum is moved away from the geometric center

formulas.torqueDef: Definition of torque: perpendicular lever arm times gravitational force
formulas.equilibriumLaw: Rotational equilibrium: clockwise torques equal counter-clockwise torques
formulas.archimedesLaw: Archimedes' law of the lever for concentrated point loads
formulas.rotationalDynamics: Newton's second law for rotation: net torque equals moment of inertia times angular acceleration

realMode.beamMassEffect: Influence of beam dead weight in overall rotational balance
realMode.pivotOffsetEffect: Fulcrum offset introduces a self-centering or tilting gravitational moment
realMode.bearingFriction: Mechanical bearing friction providing rotational oscillation damping

guided.step1Title: Step 1: Test Symmetry with Equal Masses
guided.step1Desc: Run with 'Equal Masses & Arms'. Notice how identical masses at equal distances create zero net torque and keep the beam level.
guided.step2Title: Step 2: Archimedes' Lever Principle with Unequal Masses
guided.step2Desc: Select 'Archimedes Balance'. A 4 kg mass at 1.5 m perfectly balances a 2 kg mass at 3.0 m because 4×1.5 = 2×3 = 6.
guided.step3Desc: Select 'Shifted Fulcrum' and observe how the dead weight of the beam produces an intrinsic torque when the pivot is off-center.
